conventions.convention: Signature is (−,+,+,+); spacetime orientation is independent of time orientation. The future-normal convention is K(X,Y)=g(∇_X n,Y).
In a positively oriented future-normal orthonormal tetrad, ε123=1, e_i=F(e_i,n), F_0i=−e_i, and F_ij=ε_ijk b_k. In SI interpretation e=E/c and b=B both have units tesla.
The Maxwell stress is μ₀⁻¹(F_ac F_b{}^c−g_ab F_cd F^cd/4), with sourced divergence convention ∇_a F^ab=−μ₀J^b. Consequently its stress exchange is −F_bc J^c.
The Lorentzian Hodge star is defined by α∧⋆β=⟨α,β⟩g vol_g; on two-forms ⋆²=−id and (⋆F)_ab=vol_abcd F^cd/2.

Periodic Sobolev variables use θ on R³/(2πZ)³; length coordinates are X=L₀θ. Metric and curvature arrays use the length-coordinate frame, while electric and magnetic arrays use the oriented Gram–Schmidt orthonormal frame. The two component conventions have equivalent stated Sobolev regularity.
The periodic existence and continuation arguments assume Countable Choice and integer s≥5. The smooth geometric and maximal-development arguments additionally assume Dependent Choice.

Development maximality means that every development of the same complete data embeds into the maximal development by a data-fixing, future-preserving map matching the matter fields. Geodesic completeness instead requires every maximal affinely parametrized geodesic to have domain R.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated smooth spacelike foliation and normal-frame field components, the Maxwell evolution has principal part n(e)−curl_h b and n(b)+curl_h e. Its spatial block S(ξ)(u,v)=(−C(ξ)v,C(ξ)u) is symmetric, has eigenvalues 0,0,|ξ|,|ξ|,−|ξ|,−|ξ|, and has positive coordinate time matrix α⁻¹I₆. Metric derivatives enter as lower-order coefficients; the remaining equations are the two Gauss constraints.

Assuming Countable Choice and the stated draft periodic solver, for integer s≥5 and the specified compact admissible state sets, the harmonic-reduced Einstein equations coupled to Maxwell field-strength evolution form a smooth quasilinear symmetric-hyperbolic system and have the solver's local solution and bounds for every admissible H^s initial state. No Einstein or Maxwell constraint is assumed in this reduced-system statement.

For a time-oriented C¹ Lorentzian metric and a closed real C¹ two-form on the stated smooth oriented four-manifold, ∇_a(T_EM)^a{}_b=μ₀⁻¹F_bc∇_aF^ac. Thus a continuous current satisfying ∇_aF^ab=−μ₀J^b gives ∇^aT_EM,ab=−F_bcJ^c. The stated observer energy and momentum projections also hold.

For the stated C¹ metric, C¹ two-form, C¹ spacelike foliation with an explicitly C¹ transverse future unit normal, the equations ι_n dF=ι_n d(⋆F)=0 and zero initial electric and magnetic divergences imply dF=d(⋆F)=0 near every initial point.

For the stated C³ metric, C² two-form, smooth background and spacelike foliation, harmonic-reduced Einstein evolution, normal Maxwell evolution, zero initial harmonic vector and all four initial constraints imply H=0 and the full Einstein–Maxwell equations near every initial point.

Under Countable Choice, integer s≥5, positive κ and μ₀, real Λ, periodic h∈H^(s+1) with h≥c₀I and K,e,b∈H^s satisfying the four displayed constraints have a local full source-free solution with the stated metric, metric-time-derivative and field regularities. Smooth data persist smoothly on the same base-order interval. Fixed-background reduced states have the stated bounded-class uniqueness and H^(s−1) dependence. Smooth constrained data on any smooth oriented initial three-manifold also have full developments near each initial point.

Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, the stated complete smooth oriented Einstein–Maxwell data satisfying all four constraints have a smooth development on a variable-width neighborhood of the entire initial surface, a smaller intrinsic globally hyperbolic Cauchy neighborhood, and near-surface data-fixing geometric uniqueness matching F.

Under Countable Choice and Dependent Choice, the stated nonempty connected smooth oriented constrained source-free data have a smooth connected maximal globally hyperbolic Einstein–Maxwell development universal for all smooth developments of the same complete data and unique up to a unique data-fixing future-preserving isometry matching F. No geodesic completeness or maximality among rough or non-globally-hyperbolic extensions is asserted.

alerts.finding: Clause (e) defines H⁺(S)=D⁺(S)\I⁻(D⁺(S)), then describes it as 'the set of points of D⁺(S) that are not chronologically preceded by any point of D⁺(S)'. The chronological direction is reversed: exclusion from I⁻(D⁺(S)) says that there is no q∈D⁺(S) with p≪q. Thus p does not chronologically precede any point of D⁺(S). The displayed formula and its explanatory sentence disagree; CP02 does not use this horizon clause.
